work_item.role: W1 public-evidence discovery and neutral admission

discovery_pass.method: Direction-blind admission of the committed OpenBench M3.5 correctness matrix as a distinct evidence design. The source records five concrete harnesses over the same three tasks with three trials per task, canonical gpt-5.5-medium, local execution, subscription OAuth and zero adapter errors. W1 admits the clean correctness aggregates and does not normalize the published efficiency telemetry because Codex token counts include cache reads while Cursor has no turn count.

source_known_dimensions: same three tasks: fix-failing-test, build-a-cli and make-it-run
same local execution mode on a single macOS host and run date
Devin is effort-pinned in M3.5 as gpt-5-5-medium
explicit_unknown_or_nonidentical_dimensi: historical harness package/build versions are not preserved in the M3.5 raw rows
exact upstream source revisions of the exercised harnesses
exact service-side model checkpoint behind the source model labels
independent proof that all client/provider routes resolved to an identical model snapshot
subscription/account routing and service-side state may differ by harness
client-native prompts, tools, context management and stopping behavior differ by design
ambient service-load effects are not independently controlled

non_admission_dispositions.reason: The null adapter is a benchmark calibration control rather than an exercised AI harness. Its three failed cells remain inspectable in the primary raw log but are not promoted to a harness observation.

The source explicitly states that Codex token counts include cache-read tokens while other harnesses use different token accounting, and Cursor exposes no turn count. W1 preserves the public raw telemetry as source evidence but does not create a normalized cross-harness efficiency metric or ranking.
M3 uses five trials per task and Devin without the later effort pin. It is a distinct evidence design and is not collapsed into M3.5.
